title: This Fish Shoots Flies Out of the Air From 6 Feet Away

scenes.text: This fish hits a fly six feet above the water. Without jumping.
The archerfish spits a jet of water from below the surface, and it can hit targets two meters away.
Its mouth muscles are weak. But the jet lands six times harder than the muscles could manage.
The trick: the back of the jet travels faster, so the water bunches into one slug right at the target.
It even corrects for light bending at the surface, so it aims where the fly really is.
And young fish learn it by watching older ones shoot.

description:
A fish that shoots insects out of the air from up to two meters away, without ever leaving the water.
The archerfish spits a jet of water whose tail travels faster than its head, so the water bunches into a single slug just before impact (Current Biology, 2014), hitting about six times harder than the fish's muscles alone could manage (PLoS ONE, 2012). It also corrects for the bending of light at the surface, and young fish improve by watching older ones shoot.
Which animal has the best aim in nature?
subject: archerfish
first_comment: The longer the archerfish keeps its mouth open, the farther the jet flies before it bunches into a slug, so it tunes the shot to the distance. Would you bet against it at six feet?
